subject: general
question: The latitude which passes through Alwar in Rajasthan also passes through ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sikkim is a state in northeastern India, located in the Himalayan mountains.
 
• It shares borders with Tibet in the north and northeast, Bhutan in the east, Nepal in the west, and West Bengal in the south.
 
• Despite being one of the smallest states in India, Sikkim is known for its biodiversity, including alpine and subtropical climates.
 
• The latitude passing through Alwar in Rajasthan roughly aligns with the latitude that crosses Sikkim.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Latitude:**

 
 
• Latitude is a geographic coordinate that specifies the north-south position of a point on the Earth's surface.
 
• It is an angular measurement, usually expressed in degrees (°), ranging from 0° at the Equator to 90° (North or South) at the poles.
 
• Lines of latitude are also known as parallels, and they run parallel to the Equator.
 
 
 
• **Longitude:**
 
 
• Longitude is a geographic coordinate that specifies the east-west position of a point on the Earth's surface.
 
• It is an angular measurement, usually expressed in degrees (°), ranging from 0° at the Prime Meridian to +180° eastward and -180° westward.
 
• Lines of longitude are also known as meridians, and they converge at the poles.
 
 
 
• **Geographic Coordinates:**
 
 
• Geographic coordinates are a system used to pinpoint the location of any place on Earth using latitude and longitude.
 
• This system allows for precise navigation and mapping.
 
• Coordinates are often given in degrees, minutes, and seconds, or in decimal degrees.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Mountains:**
 
 
• The Himalayas are a mountain range in Asia, separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• The range has some of the planet's highest peaks, including the very highest, Mount Everest in Nepal.
 
• The Himalayas span five countries: Bhutan, China, India, Nepal, and Pakistan.
 
• They are a crucial source of rivers and have a significant impact on the climate and ecosystem of the region.
